structured_output.hypothesis: If the Glacial period was at least partly simultaneous worldwide, globally distributed marine records dated independently of any one region will show the same glacial-stage δ18O maxima (cold, ice-rich intervals) at the same times, so that the global benthic δ18O signal and the individual regional records covary within dating error.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using the LR04 stack (Appendix 1) over 0–1.0 Ma, glacial stages (MIS 2, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20 etc.) are identified as stack δ18O maxima exceeding the 0–1 Ma mean by more than 0.5 per mil in at least 8 distinct intervals, each lasting more than 10 kyr (a very long time at each place). In addition, in at least 80% of these intervals, the individual-site records whose age models are in Appendix 3 (or the paper's Atlantic vs Pacific sub-stacks) have their δ18O maxima within ±5 kyr of the stack maximum, and the Pearson r between the stack and each regional record over 0–1 Ma is at least 0.7.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fewer than 5 glacial intervals exceed the +0.5 per mil threshold, or fewer than 50% of intervals show regional maxima within ±5 kyr of the stack maximum, or the regional-stack correlation is below 0.4. That would mean the cold phases are not synchronous across the sampled ocean basins.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'Glacial period' (multiple lines of evidence, mostly northern hemisphere and South America/New Zealand ice) is mapped to Pleistocene glacial stages. 'Temperature of the whole world simultaneously cooler' is mapped to globally coherent increases in benthic foraminiferal δ18O, which record a mix of deep-ocean temperature and ice volume. Modern reinterpretation: the test checks global synchrony of glacial maxima, not exact temperature magnitudes, and a synchrony tolerance of ±5 kyr is allowed for age-model uncertainty (the LR04 age model is itself orbitally tuned, which builds in some synchrony; this is an acknowledged limitation). Darwin's allowance for 'at least in part' simultaneous, or broad longitudinal belts, is respected: the test does not require every region to be identical.

dataset.name: Pliocene-Pleistocene stack of globally distributed benthic stable oxygen isotope records
dataset.why_it_fits: The landing page (checked) offers a ZIP of tab-delimited files: Appendix 1 (benthic δ18O stack with age), Appendix 2 (sedimentation rates), and Appendix 3 (age model conversions) from 57 globally distributed sites. Fields used: age (ka), stack δ18O, and the per-site δ18O series and ages, to test whether glacial maxima coincide across ocean basins.
